title: Threat Hunting Analyst /Information Technology Specialist 3 (Information Security), ref 5776-10AR

cond_0001.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

cond_0078.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will regularly connect with many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence to participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires the incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0078.responsibilities:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc requests, research, threat hunts, and actively assist other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events, and walk stakeholders through findings clearly.
Participate actively in projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0078.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: working as a SOC analyst, conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, participating in cyber incident response.

Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all-source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs, and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc requests, research, and threat hunts, and support other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track results, and create trends based on findings.
Classify and categorize hunting use cases based on the MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Produce daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues and ensure successful outcomes.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0214.requirements:
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Strong written communication skills and clear, direct verbal reporting, including the ability to articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving, and analytical skills.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.

Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.
cond_0235.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.
cond_0235.values: We value delivering results to a high standard and taking pride in work done well. We aim to be defined by quality, consistency, and strong performance.

cond_0236.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.

Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.

Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Execute threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Own ad-hoc requests, research, and threat hunts, and direct support to other business units as needed.
Drive the creation of detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track findings, and build trends based on results.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Deliver daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Produce technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Lead participation in active projects to identify and resolve issues/problems and ensure successful outcomes.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0242.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.

cond_0243.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, you will work alongside colleagues in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center as a Threat Hunting Analyst. In this role, you will coordinate with the team to leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to support both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will also participate with others in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to help identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc requests, research, threat hunts, and actively connect with other business units as needed to assist.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events, and walk stakeholders through findings clearly.
Participate actively in projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0249.requirements:
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.

You will coordinate with the team to leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to support both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will work alongside colleagues to help with the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires the ability to work with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0270.responsibilities:
Monitor and share reports on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all-source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs, and warnings, coordinating findings with relevant team members.
Work with the team to perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to help ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Help identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc requests and research, support threat hunts, and assist other business units as needed.
Collaborate on creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track results, and work with the team to create trends based on findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on the MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Contribute to daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues and ensure successful outcomes.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0270.requirements:
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.

Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities. cond_0299.requirements:
Bachelor's degree required, with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; advanced degree strongly preferred. Demonstrated expertise of at least two years in information technology, including a minimum of one year of proven, hands-on information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: Bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Active certification in one or more of the following is strongly preferred: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO). cond_0307.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0307.responsibilities:
Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.
cond_0307.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.
cond_0307.values: We value delivering results to a high standard and taking pride in work done well. We aim to be defined by quality, consistency, and strong performance.

The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will regularly connect with many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence to participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires the incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0330.responsibilities:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc requests, research, threat hunts, and actively assist other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events, and walk stakeholders through findings clearly.
Participate actively in projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0330.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: working as a SOC analyst, conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, participating in cyber incident response.

The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
Duties include, but are not limited to:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.
cond_0388.requirements:
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.

cond_0412.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0443.responsibilities:
Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities. Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings. Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats. Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets. Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed. Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings. Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings. Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain. Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs. Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events. Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved. Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0443.requirements:
Bachelor's degree required, with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; advanced degree strongly preferred. Demonstrated expertise of at least two years in information technology, including a minimum of one year of proven, hands-on information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: Bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Active certification in one or more of the following is strongly preferred: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO). Proven track record of 1+ years in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response. Advanced knowledge of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls). Deep knowledge of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc. Exceptional oral and written communication skills, including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding. Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving, and strong analytical abilities.

Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all-source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs, and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to support a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc requests, research tasks, and threat hunts; provide support to other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track results, and create trends based on findings.
Classify and categorize hunting use cases based on the MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Produce daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Contribute to active projects to help identify and resolve issues and ensure successful outcomes.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0457.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology, and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Strong written communication skills and clear, direct verbal reporting, including the ability to articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving, and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years of experience in one or more of the following: working as a SOC analyst, conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, or participating in cyber incident response.

cond_0458.intro:

You will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to execute both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will lead the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources.

cond_0465.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center. The role involves regular engagement with a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will stay in active contact with many third parties — such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources — to support the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires the incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0465.responsibilities:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc requests, research, threat hunts, and actively connect with other business units as needed to assist.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events, and walk stakeholders through findings clearly.
Participate actively in projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.

Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, you will work as a Threat Hunting Analyst in the [Location masked] Security Operations Center. You will coordinate with the team to leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to support both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will work alongside colleagues to help with the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires the ability to work with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0486.responsibilities:
Monitor and share reports on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all-source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs, and warnings, coordinating findings with relevant team members.
Work with the team to perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to help ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Help identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc requests and research, support threat hunts, and assist other business units as needed.
Collaborate on creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunts, track results, and work with the team to create trends based on findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on the MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Contribute to daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues and ensure successful outcomes.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
cond_0486.requirements:
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.

The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction. Most people become stronger in threat hunting and analysis over time as they build experience and learn from real-world incidents.
cond_0563.responsibilities:
Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities.
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings.
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats.
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets.
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed.
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings.
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings.
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain.
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs.
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events.
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved.
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.
cond_0563.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.

The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0642.responsibilities:
Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities. Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings. Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats. Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets. Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed. Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings. Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings. Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain. Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs. Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events. Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved. Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.
cond_0642.requirements:
A Bachelor's degree in any field, with around 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology, or equivalent practical experience; and around two years of information technology experience, including around one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: Bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology may qualify with an additional year of general information technology experience. Relevant information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following are valued, or a willingness to obtain: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO). Around 1 year of experience in one or more of the following: working as a SOC analyst, conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, participating in cyber incident response.
Background in enterprise IT environments, including areas such as system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls). Familiarity with the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Ability to communicate clearly in both oral and written form, including explaining information technology and information security concepts to varied audiences. Ability to think critically, solve problems, and approach challenges analytically. We consider candidates holistically and value relevant experience and a willingness to learn alongside formal credentials.
